title: Hashline
body:
Proofs of what an AI did, without the data


Demo  ·  November 2026  ·  Victor Rielly

caption: A demo social app. Every post is labelled by a real AI safety classifier (Mistral's open Shieldstral-1.0-3B) for explicit content, violence and hate.
Each label comes with a zero-knowledge proof that this classifier, run on this post, produced this verdict. Checking it never requires the post or the model's internal steps.
One proof per category, under a fixed registered policy and threshold. Proved once, when the post is created; the proof then travels with the post.
Proof records are batched and anchored on a public chain: Base Sepolia testnet, block 52,373,745 (test ETH only).

title: The same prover on a GPU
body:
One Llama-3-8B-sized layer, 128 hidden tokens:
	Laptop CPU	12.3 s
	Mac CPU (32 cores)	4.66 s
	Apple M3 Ultra GPU	0.36 s

≈ 11 proved tokens/s per request  ·  ≈ 22 with several at once
Next: NVIDIA GPUs, aiming at 50 tokens/s for an 8B model on one card
footnote: Measured per layer with synthetic weights at the true 8B shape; whole-model rates are computed from it.

title: What is and isn't claimed
body:
•  Hidden: inputs, outputs and every intermediate activation
•  Soundness ≈ 97 bits per run, checked by independent internal reviews
•  Privacy statements accepted after internal review; an external audit is next
•  This classifier's privacy statement is still pending, as the app's banner says
•  The app's proofs ran on a laptop CPU, minutes per category
